name: Vanthorpe Selvedge Henley
description:
A three-button henley in heavyweight cotton-analog weave, the kind of shirt that feels broken in from the first wear. Vanthorpe sources their selvedge from a mill cooperative in what used to be the Carolinas, and the fabric has that slight irregularity of something woven slowly — a faint salt-and-pepper texture in a range of muted earth tones. The placket buttons are matte bone resin. Chest seams sit flat and clean. Comes in sizes that actually fit augmented shoulder profiles without bunching.

This is a working person's shirt that also happens to be genuinely good. Machinists, transit engineers, dockworkers on Lake Erie wear it because it lasts. It also gets picked up by Tier 3 folks who like the honest craftsmanship aesthetic — the shirt that says you don't need to perform effort because you actually do the work.
what_it_says: You value durability over flash. You either work with your hands or want people to think you do, and in this case the shirt earns the read either way.
story_hooks: A Vanthorpe henley with a specific dye lot number has become an identifying mark among a network of labor organizers — the shirt itself is a signal.
The Carolina mill cooperative that weaves the fabric is rumored to be operating in a corponation dead zone, outside any charter — someone wants to know who's actually running it.
A character finds a henley in a dead man's locker; the chest pocket has been carefully unpicked and re-sewn around a folded piece of paper.

physical_description.visual_profile: A classic henley silhouette with understated sophistication—neither aggressively casual nor formally fitted. The shirt sits naturally on the shoulders with a slight taper through the torso, projecting quiet competence rather than aspirational style. The three-button placket breaks the neckline without formality.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the chest and shoulders with enough structure to accommodate augmented profiles without bunching or gapping. Sleeves taper gently from shoulder to wrist without constraining movement. Length reaches mid-hip, appropriate for both tucking and wearing loose.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavyweight cotton-analog weave sourced from Carolina mill cooperatives—a synthetic-natural blend that mimics heritage denim construction but with softer hand-feel. The selvedge edge remains visible on the side seams as a mark of slow-loom authenticity.
physical_description.texture: Nuanced salt-and-pepper weave with subtle irregularities from traditional production methods. The surface reads slightly nubby and organic under close inspection, with a soft nap that catches light unevenly. Faint horizontal texture from the weaving process is visible on closer examination.
physical_description.color_scheme: Muted earth tone palette—warm grays, faded khakis, dusty browns, and charcoal accents. The color shifting within individual pieces reflects the irregular dyeing of heritage cotton-analog. No aggressive contrast or logos.
physical_description.closures: Three matte bone-resin buttons down the placket. Buttons are slightly recessed and feature subtle organic texture—the kind that feels substantial without drawing attention.
distinctive_features: Selvedge trim visible on side seams
Flat, clean chest seams engineered for augmented shoulder profiles
Matte bone-resin buttons with organic surface detail
Intentional fabric irregularities from slow-loom production
Heritage mill cooperative branding embossed (not printed) on interior tag
Reinforced stress points at shoulder and armpit seams
Slight color variation between garments reflecting dye-lot authenticity
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 aspirational—genuinely functional workwear that reads as quality craftsmanship without Tier 1 price-tag performance tech. The aesthetic appeal to Tier 2 professionals is secondary; the primary audience is working-class who recognize lasting construction.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by machinists, transit engineers, dock workers, and anyone whose labor is hands-on and skilled. The shirt signals 'I don't perform work—I do work.' Also adopted by Tier 3 aesthetes who value honest construction over performative luxury. Worn in Lake Erie industrial zones, manufacturing districts, and repair shops. Occasionally styled by corpo-adjacent Tier 2 workers attempting accessible authenticity.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in from first wear, with a softness that increases with washing. Develops natural creasing at the elbows and shoulders. Over years, may show faded areas where worn frequently, softened hem edges, and a deepened patina that reads as earned rather than distressed.

image_prompt: Close-up fashion photograph of a Vanthorpe Selvedge Henley draped on a dark matte mannequin torso, angled to show the three-button placket and chest seaming detail. The fabric's salt-and-pepper weave texture is prominent under warm industrial lighting casting subtle shadows across the nubby surface. Muted earth-tone fabric catches sidelight, revealing the heritage cotton-analog's irregular weave pattern. Matte bone-resin buttons reflect minimal light.
